Agent Runtime is a general agent API that can connect to different services. It uses the caller's permissions to restrict RAG search, MCP tools, Skills, and Agents, and uses only allowed capabilities to produce answers. During a chat, it can organize drafts and intermediate analysis in a private, thread-specific /workspace. The answer is delivered in the chat body.

A service integrating with Agent Runtime usually follows these steps: Read /v1/models and /v1/indices to obtain model and index values. Prepare user_id, chat_id, x_request_id, and a send_system_name appropriate to the caller. When CALLER_AUTH_ENABLED=true, System/Sub Frontend and personal callers need an active binding key, except for exact trusted Admin senders. Issue a send_system_name key to register a new System; no separate allowlist setting is needed. Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming or non-streaming transport and handle finish_reason and the HTTP error envelope according to the transport contract. Let the runtime apply the resolved permission_groups and index to MCP/Skills/Agents rather than calling those assets directly. For operations, find the run_id through /v1/runs and read its detail/evidence. The same chat_id preserves conversation checkpoints, HITL, and /workspace. The same user_id owns long-term Memory and past conversations. Deployments can select caller authentication, Permission API integration, builtin search, and personalization. With personalization OFF, conversation history and past-conversation lookup remain available, and users can explicitly request Memory deletion. Fixed server messages use DEFAULT_LOCALE=ko|en; time handling uses TIMEZONE. Switch this documentation site's language independently through the 한국어/English menu. Documentation deployment root is selected by DOCS_ROOT_LOCALE=ko|en, default ko. TIMEZONE is fixed at initial deployment; other regions use independent installations.

Agent Runtime's Chat endpoint constructs a DeepAgents runtime using each request's identity, permission groups, and indices. It uses only permitted MCP tools, Skills, and Agents. Agent assets extend Main's capabilities. Users do not select or call them directly; the runtime exposes relevant assets using /v1/chat/completions orch metadata and service settings.

Asset Role Reference MCP Servers/tools for retrieval, deep search, and external execution. MCP Skills Instruction bundles for working methods or review criteria. Skills Agents Subagent definitions for focused review/analysis. Agents

Operators put physical assets in assets/skills/ and assets/agents/. Agents see virtual roots tailored to the request's owner and permissions, rather than host paths. Agent-visible path Content Access and lifetime /workspace Drafts, intermediate analysis, and shared Main/Subagent working files Read/write/edit only within the current user_id:chat_id thread, persisted in PostgreSQL checkpoints. /runtime Native conversation archives and framework-owned artifacts Thread-private and checkpoint-backed. Only the framework writes. Models can read exact conversation-provided paths under /runtime/conversation_history/<artifact> or /runtime/large_tool_results/<artifact>. /memories The current user_id's /memories/MEMORY.md User-scoped and read-only when personalization is ON. OFF blocks automatic loading, prompt injection, and ordinary file reads. /skills Permitted physical assets/skills definitions Read-only. /agents Permitted physical assets/agents definitions Read-only. For example, user A's /workspace/notes.md in chat 1 remains readable by later requests in that chat and another API process, but not by A's chat 2 or user B. The pod's physical /, assets/mcp_server.json, and other host files are not mounted. Shell/execute is unavailable. Agents cannot modify /memories, /skills, or /agents. /runtime is separate from workspace quotas and is not a general working directory. Its root, arbitrary namespaces, relative paths, and traversal are not readable. Agents use ls, glob, grep, read_file, write_file, and edit_file as needed. Reading a Skill produces [Skill] progress; other filesystem work produces [Tool] <tool>. Workspace files are internal working material: the Agent must deliver the requested result in the final chat body, rather than merely naming a path. Hiding detailed progress preserves execution and permission checks. Personalization OFF retains existing Memory, conversation history, and past-conversation lookup. Users can explicitly delete Memory through Main's dedicated tool, which does not delete conversation history, summaries, or checkpoints.

Different permission_groups can expose different capabilities for the same question. Target Filtering MCP server Its access.permission_groups checks the request groups. Skill SKILL.md frontmatter access.permission_groups applies. Agent Agent Markdown frontmatter access.permission_groups applies. Virtual filesystem Only permitted Skills/Agents appear under /skills and /agents. /workspace and framework-owned /runtime are thread-isolated. GET /v1/manifest exposes MCP tools, Skills, and Agents so a Router can understand the service. It is a static inventory without a per-user permission body. Per-request visibility based on access.permission_groups is determined by Chat. Restricted Skill/Agent names and descriptions may therefore appear in the manifest. It is not a metadata security boundary. Do not put credentials, sensitive internal information, or permission-protected content in descriptions.

Recommended Avoid Generate stable orch.identity.user_id, chat_id, and x_request_id. Reusing a request ID for a different user request. Supply the appropriate sender and active binding key when auth is ON. Using a System key as a personal key, or claiming System identity with a personal key. Render hitl as a user question. Discarding the interrupted chat_id and starting a new chat. Read /v1/manifest to understand service scope. Directly invoking MCP tools, Skill files, or Agents. Read operational evidence through /v1/runs*. Expecting raw provider traces or private reasoning in API responses. MCP tools, Skills, Main/Subagents, and model calls are recorded as Langfuse observations. Inspect each observation's input/output and its containing agent node in Runs evidence to identify execution ownership. Public responses remove framework metadata/internal IDs and express ownership through nesting. Turn Evaluation is not an Agent execution observation and is excluded from evidence. It remains in terminal Langfuse run.artifact.output.turn_evaluation. An empty array means it did not execute; a failed evaluation leaves a record with completion_status="failed" and a safe failure_reason. enabled=false excludes an MCP from both runtime and manifest. includeInManifest=false retains Chat availability but hides Router inventory.

Startup validates required and conditional settings. Changes require restart. New booleans accept trimmed, case-insensitive true/false only; unset uses the default, while blank/other values are errors. OFF preserves body, heartbeat, compaction, actual HITL, and required errors. Turn Evaluation replaces the former Continuation Gate retry budget. complete permits Memory/summary postprocessing; needs_revision returns to the compiled Main model within the revision budget. Initial and revised answers stream immediately. Processing progress appears only before an actual revision and is hidden with details OFF. One Main invocation's chunks concatenate unchanged; distinct valid blocks receive the needed blank line consistently in SSE, terminal, non-stream, and storage. Internal evaluation instructions never enter the user answer. Evaluation uses a fixed 30-second overall budget for initial request, JSON/schema validation, optional repair, and automatic Memory planning, independently of LLM_TIMEOUT. Timeout, Internal LLM failure, or critical schema failure preserves the latest Main answer and skips revision/persistence. Memory and conversation-summary decisions validate independently: one invalid side effect does not discard a valid completion/revision decision. Without compaction, the evaluator reads the current turn's raw user/model/tool/final execution. With compaction, it reads the effective summary projection plus raw execution after the cutoff, without reinjecting large pre-compaction results. Summary may support completion/conversation summary, but is not direct evidence for new Memory facts.

DeepAgents 0.7.15 native SummarizationMiddleware compacts long context. Raw messages remain canonical checkpoint history. Messages before _summarization_event.cutoff_index project as a summary HumanMessage(lc_source="summarization"); recent tail stays raw. Native partitioning preserves the latest user input and unfinished Tool/HITL protocol. There is no compaction environment knob. Catalog max_input_tokens declares gateway input capacity and maps directly to the identically named LangChain profile. DeepAgents uses its native 85% trigger and 10% keep window. Provider max_tokens is an output-generation parameter, unrelated to input capability. Summary input is bounded to 4K tokens. Native selection uses last, start_on=human, and partial/system inclusion. Only if that returns empty is the start_on constraint removed with the same budget/direction to permit tool tails. Selection errors propagate as context_compaction_failed, not empty success. Small thresholds belong only in test-owned fixtures, never production configuration. The event stores cutoff, summary message, and archive path; it does not physically replace raw checkpoint messages. Model input becomes: Native effective context single system → HumanMessage(lc_source=summarization) → recent tail after cutoff → current request Raw compacted history is archived privately under /runtime/conversation_history/**. The summary points to that archive. If both primary/fallback selections are empty, no fake summary is created. Successful archive storage permits archive-only continuation with recent tail and targeted grep/offset-limited read_file recovery. The full archive is not injected by default; storage failure does not record a successful event/cutoff. The summary invocation is named compaction and uses the Main model. Native usage checks the latest effective AIMessage; fresh post-compaction usage can trigger again even with a small approximate count. Empty model summaries and provider/ selection failures terminate explicitly as context_compaction_failed. Large tool results use native offload to /runtime/large_tool_results/<tool-call-id> with a bounded preview and recovery path. grep and limited reads recover needed details. Runtime artifacts do not consume workspace quota; models cannot write/edit them. Retriever/Deep Search use the same native policy without an additional character limit. Streaming announces compaction. Completed cycles rearm only after actual Main content/tool/Skill/Agent work; summarizer activity, empty model events, and heartbeat do not rearm. Summary token streams remain private, and non-stream/artifact structure is unchanged. Compaction progress Summarizing earlier messages as the conversation grows. Situation Physical model calls Short request One answer One summary unit One summary + one answer Provider overflow recovery Failed answer + summary + retried answer Multiple summary units/rolling merge One call per summary unit + answer model ├─ compaction (Chain) │ └─ ChatOpenAI (Generation) └─ ChatOpenAI (Generation) compaction identifies the summary model; its provider Generation can appear as a child. The subsequent Generation is Main continuing with compacted context. No extra ChatOpenAI Chain is inserted between compaction and its Generation. Summary calls rebuild gateway headers from the current Main ModelRequest: User-Id, User-Type, Chat-Id, fresh Prompt-Msg-Id, X-dep-ticket, api-key, Send-System-Name, and Accept. Missing required request context fails explicitly before calling the provider. Compaction summary failure fallback The conversation could not be summarized. Please try again shortly. Large routed history is deduplicated against the checkpoint and appended as a new suffix rather than rejected merely at the trigger. Failed-request retries do not append already-checkpointed user messages. Checkpoint read failure is explicit, never treated as empty history. Overflow remaining after forced compaction has finish_reason=error, loop.stop_reason=context_overflow; oversized latest user input must be split. Summary failures use context_compaction_failed.

Service identity, search policy, and filesystem rules remain in configs/system_prompt.jinja2. Harness Profile is an official middleware extension point, not a second hardcoded prompt policy. A caller's single system text stays request-local configurable data. Main middleware appends an authority wrapper and a JSON-string serialized instruction after the service runtime context. Serialization separates structure from caller text; it does not erase instruction meaning. Subagents do not include this middleware, and Evaluator/compactor use separate internal boundaries. Nothing persists into messages/checkpoints or silently carries into later requests/resumes. Runtime resolves the Main/subagent model profile, excludes default native summarization, and explicitly installs configured graph middleware. It does not temporarily mutate a library-global factory during concurrent compilation. Prompt and middleware composition configs/system_prompt.jinja2 + service-owned request/runtime context + current request requester instruction (Main Agent only) + model Harness Profile: exclude native summarization + graph middleware: explicitly install configured compaction middleware = main/subagent runtime Potential future profile capabilities do not justify moving current policy or adding model-name branches. Only concrete, agreed model differences belong in profiles.

What execution appears in evidence?​ No separate tool-selection list exists in MCP configuration. Recorded Main/subagent, model, MCP/tool, Skill, guardrail, HITL, and errors appear as semantic evidence. Tool outputs are JSON-safe, and failed observations retain error.message rather than disappearing. Unrecorded provider-private reasoning cannot be reconstructed. Evaluation is not a graph execution node. Validated responses/failure records stay in ordered run.artifact.output.turn_evaluation. Unconfigured evaluation leaves an empty array; failure records have completion_status="failed", persistence no-op values, and stable failure_reason, without raw exceptions, provider bodies, prompts, or Memory content. Why do x_request_id and Prompt-Msg-Id differ?​ The former identifies one caller request; the latter separates each physical LLM call within it. Never copy the inbound request ID into outbound provider IDs. Chat-Id groups calls belonging to one conversation.

Setting Required Default Responsibility STREAM_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL No 15 Visible idle heartbeat; greater than 0 and at most 55 seconds, below frontend idle timeout. Request stream defaults to true: true sends SSE and false returns one JSON result from the same execution and content/storage assembly. Detailed progress affects SSE notices only. Main/Subagent internal model streaming and structured Internal LLM non-stream calls remain unchanged. Zero is not a heartbeat OFF value. Locale controls its fixed wording. Preparation idle carries into streaming and only actual post-filter output resets it. Heartbeat may precede the first answer and stops after terminal/HITL/error/cancellation. Existing correlated logs/traces separate preparation, MCP wait/discovery, compile, first model signal, tool duration, first real visible output, and heartbeat count. Heartbeat is excluded from first real-output timing. Does HTTP 200 mean streaming succeeded?​ No. Failure after response start has terminal finish_reason=error; HITL has hitl and awaits input. Inspect terminal reason, not just HTTP status or [DONE]. Non-stream Agent failure instead returns HTTP 500 error envelope.
Setting Required Default Responsibility MCP_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT No 5 Per-server discovery budget to isolate slow dependencies. PROBE_TIMEOUT No 5 Overall Probe RAG/rerank dependency budget.

Setting Required Default Responsibility INTERNAL_LLM_BASE_URL Conditional None Auxiliary gateway for evaluation/search rewriting. INTERNAL_LLM_MODEL Conditional None Auxiliary model. INTERNAL_LLM_X_DEP_TICKET Conditional None Independent credential, never Main ticket fallback. Personalization ON requires all three values before accepting requests. With OFF, an empty group skips evaluator/new model summaries while preserving records and lookup; a complete group still supports completion evaluation and summaries. Evaluation, shared Memory planning, and Deep Search rewriting/decomposition use this gateway. Connection/auth/model/HTTP/headers are shared, and every Internal LLM call uses stream:false. Each use case owns its prompt, body, schema, generation options, repair, and fallback policy. Official OpenAI endpoints receive Bearer auth and compatible structured JSON schema while retaining gateway headers. Initial/repair structured requests explicitly use stream:false; they are not streaming Internal LLM operations. Missing/failed evaluation preserves the answer and skips postprocessing. Deep Search gateway failure falls back to original-question rule planning, with reason in diagnostics.plan.fallback_reason and the tool's evidence output.

/v1/models reads public IDs from the active catalog: Model catalog { "models": [ { "model": "GaussO4.1-260330", "base_url": "https://llm-gateway.example/v1", "max_input_tokens": 262144 }, { "model": "Gemma4-260430", "base_url": "https://another-llm-gateway.example/v1", "max_input_tokens": 262144 } ] } max_input_tokens is input capacity, mapped directly to the LangChain profile, not an output-generation parameter. Catalog does not hold provider names or generation config. Main/Evaluator/Deep Search use the Chat Completions-compatible boundary; each use case owns its schemas and generation settings.

RAG and DS settings accept CSV. tip After changing public RAG_INDEX, restart and inspect /v1/indices before updating the frontend selection/allowlist. Index environment RAG_INDEX=rag-index,example-index DS_INDEX=ds-index The catalog exposes public RAG indices only. Chat selects allowlisted intersections; Search Proxy requires every requested index to be in the list.

Tables are isolated in the service schema. The DBA prepares standards.usage_log_base and inherited <SERVICE_NAME>.<SERVICE_NAME> with columns, constraints, and indices. Startup validates this contract without altering the child, then prepares API-owned tables, checkpointer, and Store in that schema. Checkpoint handles continuity, Store handles user Memory, and hitl_pending handles waiting; no duplicate sessions/run_state table is created. Area Table Responsibility HITL hitl_pending Awaiting question/answer state Session lock session_locks Lease preventing concurrent user/chat work Run summary run_index Safe Runs list index Conversation summary conversation_summary Per-user/chat encrypted title/summary and timestamps; no embedding/keywords API Key api_keys HMAC, binding, expiry/revocation; no raw secrets Permission cache permission_cache API role values by user, external ad_id name retained; 3-hour TTL, not merged groups DBA-owned Usage <SERVICE_NAME>.<SERVICE_NAME> Chat ledger; final groups on success, rejected/error/NULL groups on auth failure Memory store, store_migrations LangGraph user Memory; encrypted value.content Checkpoint checkpoints Thread graph state Typed payload checkpoint_blobs New writes have +aes type suffix Intermediate writes checkpoint_writes New writes have +aes suffix Checkpoint schema checkpoint_migrations Preparation version HITL session ID is an independent primary key, not a session-table FK. The same user/chat identity joins checkpoint, lock, and pending state. Persisted interaction_id, last_run_id, and next_phase_index survive restart. Row existence means pending; payload owns question/reask while checkpoint owns answers/tool state.

Choose TIMEZONE at first deployment and retain it during operation. Existing Korean services use an unset value or Asia/Seoul with their existing Usage defaults. Usage rows, KST Memory dates, checkpoints, Runs, and conversation summaries are not rewritten; no timezone migration CLI is needed. Other regions use independent new deployments/storage. The DBA preserves shared standards.usage_log_base types/defaults and other services. Prepare the new child's complete columns, inheritance, constraints, and indexes, then align only that child's created_at default with its region. For an already prepared US West child: New US West service child default ALTER TABLE agent_runtime_us_west.agent_runtime_us_west ALTER COLUMN created_at SET DEFAULT (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'); Deploy with SERVICE_NAME=agent_runtime_us_west and TIMEZONE=America/Los_Angeles. Startup rejects mismatched child defaults without automatically altering tables. Keep existing Korean child defaults as now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Seoul'. Connections apply the service search path and TIMEZONE. Older connections did not override session timezone; confirm their actual DBA environment with SHOW TimeZone. Aware inputs, timestamptz, and explicit regional conversions preserve instants despite session display changes. API dates use the request application's TIMEZONE and retain explicit offsets' instants. Naive Usage timestamps store local wall clocks and cannot distinguish the two instants in a repeated DST hour. Use existing timestamptz execution records for precise chronology, ordering, and elapsed analysis. Ambiguous/nonexistent API input requires an explicit offset.

Service names begin with lowercase letter or _, then lowercase letters, digits, or _, at most 63 bytes. Schema-qualified names are unsupported. danger Do not use public.usage_logs as the service name or duplicate search-path options in the DSN. Main, checkpoint, Store, and sync connections receive the service path and configured timezone from the application. Column Responsibility request_id Correlation/dedup dedup_scope Normally user/chat session dedup_result accepted, duplicate, not_applied user_id Requester identity chat_id Business conversation created_at Naive wall-clock in TIMEZONE; align the service child default with its region model Requested model index_name Requested search index permission_groups Effective groups or NULL on auth failure upstream_name Controlled sender/source projection stream Transport status accepted, rejected, completed, hitl_pending, failed, cancelled http_status Status delivered to caller error_message Safe public error internal_error Redacted diagnostic JSON No endpoint/operation columns exist in the Chat-only ledger. Manifest/Probe/Search use logs/traces without Usage rows. Source projection: Sender Routing Stored source Missing/blank/null/api Any api ds_assistant Enabled ds_assistant ds_assistant Missing/false-like Current SERVICE_NAME Other trusted Any Trimmed sender Non-admin/non-reserved System Any Trimmed sender Trusted _test/reserved System Any invalid_send_system_name User IDs remain normalized opaque values, even when authorization fails.

Examples use SERVICE_NAME=agent_runtime; the tables below illustrate one request row rather than a full database dump. 1. Successful non-stream Chat​ The row is accepted before work and updated after response determination. Column Example Meaning request_id 896cd7ad-8e3c-4c85-b918-a294d133c44e One user question dedup_scope employee.one:2b0e1c88-540d-4af7-85d8-b1e7f6fa865e User/chat dedup boundary dedup_result accepted Actual execution user_id employee.one Requester chat_id 2b0e1c88-540d-4af7-85d8-b1e7f6fa865e Thread model GaussO4.1-260330 Payload model index_name rag-index Payload index permission_groups {EXAMPLE_REVIEWERS} Effective merged permissions upstream_name api Direct caller without sender stream false Non-stream status / http_status completed / 200 Successful answer error_message / internal_error NULL / NULL No error This means the user's question ran once and returned normally. 2. Successful streaming Chat​ stream=true; HTTP 200 starts first, and successful terminal delivery establishes completed. Failure after start can still have HTTP 200, so inspect status too. Final loop information is in Chat terminal and Runs detail. 3. Chat waiting for HITL​ Usage is hitl_pending, HTTP 200, no error. A pending row shares the session ID. Resume preserves chat and creates a new request ID. Even after compaction, pending row/checkpoint interrupt—not summary prose—decides resume. 4. Repeated request​ Same scope/request ID does not execute again. The original accepted row stays; a separate duplicate attempt has dedup_result=duplicate, status=rejected, HTTP 409, and a safe duplicate error. Frequent rows may indicate duplicate UI submits or incorrectly reused retry IDs. 5. Invalid identity/UUID​ Missing orch, blank/placeholder user, or nil IDs return 400 invalid_identity; malformed UUID schema returns 422 validation_error. Dots are not validated. Usage is not_applied/rejected with the safe error, without model/RAG/MCP work. 6. Previous stream still active​ Session conflict is rejected, HTTP 409, with dedup_result=accepted or not_applied because the ID may be new. Wait for the previous stream. Duplicate means request-ID collision; conflict means concurrent work in one conversation. 7. Manifest, Probe, Search​ These create no Usage rows. Search X-Request-Id and Probe metadata.x_request_id still correlate responses/logs, but do not identify Chat ledger rows. Repeated Probe payloads both execute workload; there is no separate idempotency store for these APIs. 8. Connection lost during delivery​ Situation Usage status HTTP Before response start cancelled NULL After response start, body incomplete cancelled Started status, often 200 Terminal delivered; only [DONE] failed Preserve terminal status 200 Cancellation may be browser refresh, network loss, or caller timeout, not an application defect. 9. Joining Usage and run summaries​ Usage explains inbound request/HTTP outcome; run_index discovers safe user runs; Langfuse detail/evidence explains nested execution and input/output. Detail first checks PG existence/terminal state, then reads the exact run trace's matching run.artifact and observations. running appears in list but returns 409 run_not_terminal in detail/evidence. The observability section explains evaluation and filtering. Recent usage logs SELECT created_at, upstream_name, status, http_status, request_id FROM agent_runtime.agent_runtime WHERE user_id = 'employee.one' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20; Recent run summaries SELECT run_id, interaction_id, parent_run_id, phase_index, created_at, status, model, stream, request_id FROM run_index WHERE user_id = 'employee.one' ORDER BY created_at DESC, run_id DESC LIMIT 20; Match user, chat, and request IDs to connect outcomes. Common queries: Usage status counts SELECT upstream_name, status, http_status, count(*) FROM agent_runtime.agent_runtime WHERE created_at >= now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Seoul' - interval '1 day' GROUP BY upstream_name, status, http_status ORDER BY count(*) DESC; User usage history SELECT created_at, upstream_name, user_id, chat_id, request_id, status, error_message FROM agent_runtime.agent_runtime WHERE user_id = 'employee.one' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50; User run history SELECT run_id, user_id, chat_id, request_id, created_at, status, model, stream, interaction_id, parent_run_id, phase_index FROM run_index WHERE user_id = 'employee.one' ORDER BY created_at DESC, run_id DESC LIMIT 20; Deduplication lookup SELECT dedup_scope, request_id, status, http_status, created_at FROM agent_runtime.agent_runtime WHERE dedup_scope IS NOT NULL AND request_id = '896cd7ad-8e3c-4c85-b918-a294d133c44e' ORDER BY created_at DESC;

MCP, Skills, and Agents live under AGENTIC_ASSETS_DIR. warning Files are not hot-reloaded. Restart after configuration/Skill/Agent changes, then inspect /v1/manifest. Asset directory assets/ mcp_server.json skills/ evidence-review/ SKILL.md agents/ evidence-reviewer.md

Physical deployment assets differ from model-visible routes: Virtual route Backend Contract /workspace/** Quota-aware StateBackend User/chat thread, Main/subagent shared, checkpointed /runtime/conversation_history/** Private runtime state Exact allowed archive reads; framework-only writes; separate quota Other /runtime/** Private runtime state Deny arbitrary model reads/writes; restored by thread checkpoint /memories/MEMORY.md Store-backed Memory User read-only when personalization ON; ordinary access denied OFF, explicit deletion retained /skills/** Permission-filtered assets Allowed read-only Skills /agents/** Permission-filtered assets Allowed read-only definitions Other paths Deny backend No host roots, MCP config, or unrouted assets Native tools are ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, and subagent task. Writes/edits are allowed only in workspace. No shell/execute. Tool permissions and backend traversal/read-only checks both enforce boundaries. Runtime is not an arbitrary model-created workspace. Quota measures UTF-8 bytes. Default per-file 512 KiB/thread 2 MiB failures return workspace_quota_exceeded without silently overwriting files. Both settings must be positive and file limit must not exceed total. Workspace files do not replace delivered answers. The prompt requires results in chat. Runtime conservatively continues once only if the current pass successfully wrote/edited workspace and the answer is empty or save/path-only—not merely because the body mentions a workspace path. Skill reads use [Skill], other filesystem calls [Tool], without changing SSE shape or adding progress when no file work occurs.

Register servers in mcpServers: MCP server config { "mcpServers": { "retriever": { "transport": "stdio", "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "app.mcp_servers.retriever.server"], "env": { "RAG_API_URL": "${RAG_API_URL}", "RAG_API_KEY": "${RAG_API_KEY}", "RAG_X_DEP_TICKET": "${RAG_X_DEP_TICKET}", "INDEX": "${RAG_INDEX}" }, "access": { "permission_groups": ["EXAMPLE_REVIEWERS"] }, "requestScopedInjection": { "body": [ {"from": "permission_groups", "to": "permission_groups"}, {"from": "index", "to": "index", "overwrite": false}, {"from": "request_id", "to": "request_id"}, {"from": "user_id", "to": "user_id"} ] }, "enabled": true, "includeInManifest": true }, "external_http": { "transport": "http", "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp", "requestScopedInjection": { "body": [ {"from": "permission_groups", "to": "permission_groups"}, {"from": "index", "to": "index", "overwrite": false} ], "header": [ {"from": "user_id", "to": "X-User-Id"}, {"from": "request_id", "to": "X-Request-Id"}, {"from": "chat_id", "to": "X-Chat-Id"} ] }, "enabled": true, "includeInManifest": true } } } The MCP group EXAMPLE_REVIEWERS and the Skill/Agent group ORG_PROCESS illustrate configuration, not mandatory groups. Use actual service policy. Property Contract enabled Runtime activation, default true; false fully excludes it. includeInManifest Router inventory visibility, independent of execution. requestScopedInjection Explicit body/header destinations for request fields. timeout Tool-call cap, default 60 seconds; host wrapper for stdio, also adapter connection for HTTP/streamable. sse_read_timeout Silence between events after connection, adapter default 300 seconds; optional per-server override. access.permission_groups Restricted server group intersection. Disabled entries remain configuration but disappear from loading, injection, manifest, and execution tracing. Use includeInManifest=false to hide only Router inventory while retaining runtime execution. Evidence retains actual arguments/results, excluding framework input.runtime; nesting identifies the owning Agent. Access metadata is app-owned and never sent to MCP. Absent/empty access is public; non-empty groups require intersection for exposure and execution. Injection is separate: it transfers normalized request-body or inbound-header sources into explicit body/header destinations for already permitted tools. All four directions are expressible. Header destinations apply only to HTTP/SSE MCP; write downstream names such as X-User-Id, not snake_case source names. Header comparison is case-insensitive; configuration consistently uses readable hyphenated names. Does requestScopedInjection grant permissions?​ No. It transfers data during an already authorized invocation; it cannot expose or execute a forbidden MCP. A body injection can supply RAG groups; a header injection can forward correlation metadata. Stdio call timeout is enforced by Runtime, not an SDK connection argument. HTTP uses it at adapter connection and tool wrapper. Independent per-server discovery budget prevents one slow server from blocking preparation indefinitely. Manifest is partial best-effort; first Chat discovery also isolates failed servers, with no required retriever-name contract. Chat retains per-server last-known-good definitions. The first request after 600 seconds from completed discovery refreshes registered candidates. Successful servers replace their whole set, including authoritative empty lists. Failed servers retain definitions/state. Changed name/description/schema triggers graph compilation; a candidate is adopted atomically with definitions/state. Failed compile preserves the old graph and advances the completed-attempt clock. Unchanged fingerprints still adopt recovery state. No scheduler/additional TTL/env exists. Typed connection/session failures count at server scope; per-tool timeout, confirmed stale tool/schema, and backend errors count at tool scope. Two consecutive failures block exposure and dispatch. Invalid arguments, normal empty success, cancellation, and HITL do not count. Classified external failures do not consume global mistake budget, while repeated forbidden calls and execution limits remain. Shared state requires the same connection/authentication scope. Fixed built-in RAG/DS connections retain failures and blocks across requests without resetting on correlation arguments. Custom dynamic request injection retains request-local isolation. Active requests pin definitions and block state; late results cannot poison a newer generation. Adopted discovery success permits new requests; failure keeps blocks until the next 600-second opportunity. Why can Manifest and Chat have different MCP tools?​ Manifest is static per-server best-effort inventory. Disabled, hidden, or failed servers may be absent while siblings remain. Chat combines currently permitted enabled servers with last-known-good state; an initially failed server is omitted without requiring a particular retriever. Timing, request permissions, and block state can therefore produce different lists. Manifest has no per-user group body, so restricted Skill/Agent descriptions may appear; Chat filters actual exposure again. Stdio python/python3 resolves to the API's interpreter, so a host virtualenv also runs child MCP with its dependencies. Explicit custom interpreter paths/launchers are retained and must contain required dependencies. sse_read_timeout measures next-event silence, not total execution; default assets use adapter 300 seconds. note Manifest visibility follows enabled/includeInManifest/discovery. Per-user runtime visibility follows access.permission_groups independently.

Directory and frontmatter name must match. tip Descriptions appear in Manifest. Use a short understandable purpose; put procedures in the body. SKILL.md --- name: evidence-review description: Review answer grounding against retrieved RAG evidence. access: permission_groups: - ORG_PROCESS --- Check whether the answer separates evidence-backed facts from inference.

Declare each Agent in assets/agents/<name>.md. info Subagents do not automatically receive the whole parent conversation. Design focused work from the task description and permitted tools/Skills. Agent definition --- name: evidence-reviewer description: Review evidence-backed answers for missing assumptions and caveats. skills: - evidence-review tools: - mcp__retriever__rag_search access: permission_groups: - ORG_PROCESS --- Review the draft answer for evidence consistency and missing caveats. Return concise private guidance to the main agent. Change Apply New Skill Add file and restart New Agent Add definition and restart MCP server entry Edit config and restart Existing MCP tool contract First request after 600 seconds since completed discovery refreshes Asset permissions Edit frontmatter/access and restart

This reference helps callers and operators choose an endpoint and understand its request and response without inspecting the implementation. Read the usage guide first for identity, permissions, index selection, and UUID generation rules.

Capability Endpoint Purpose Status GET /, GET /health, GET /metrics Check whether the server responds to HTTP requests. Model and index catalog GET /v1/models, GET /v1/indices Obtain model IDs and search indices for Chat. Chat POST /v1/chat/completions Submit a user question and receive SSE or JSON. Router GET /v1/manifest, POST /v1/probe Read service information and search evidence. Search POST /v1/search/* Forward validated search requests to the RAG API. Runs POST /v1/runs, GET /v1/runs/{run_id}, GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/evidence Read execution history, Main/Subagent nesting, and observation inputs/outputs.
