When builtin RAG is disabled or no public RAG index exists, /v1/indices returns [], and direct search/probe return 404 feature_disabled. Key management APIs return the same code when caller authentication is OFF. Disabled features are distinct from upstream integration failures.

No. Chat terminal orch.rag.source_urls, contexts, and doc_images remain empty for compatibility. Find the run_id using /v1/runs, then request GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/evidence for retrieval and tool evidence. Answer citations are in the assistant message itself.
documents.s: Does empty orch.rag mean no search occurred?

documents.t: No. Reusing an ID already accepted within the same user_id:chat_id returns 409 duplicate_request without executing the workload twice. This is not an idempotent response cache.
documents.s: Will retrying x_request_id replay the response?

documents.t: The contracts differ. Blank Chat orch.rag_params.index selects all configured public RAG indices. Search Proxy requires an explicit validated search boundary and rejects blank names, wildcards, and non-allowlisted values with 422.
documents.s: Why does Chat accept blank index while Search Proxy rejects blank index_name?

documents.t: /, /health, and /metrics are shallow process checks. They do not probe PostgreSQL, RAG, the LLM gateway, or MCP on each request. Check the public error code, correlated pod logs, and dependency health separately.
documents.s: Why can Chat fail when /health returns 200?

documents.t: With personalization ON, the same user's long-term facts and preferences may be used in a new chat. Memory is user-scoped and exposed read-only at /memories/MEMORY.md. Actual messages, HITL, and /workspace are scoped to user_id:chat_id. Other users' Memory and conversations are inaccessible. OFF blocks automatic Memory reads, injection, writes, and ordinary file access. It preserves existing Memory, records, summaries, checkpoints, and history access. Explicit full or partial deletion of the user's own Memory remains available. Partial deletion removes only relevant phrases and preserves the remaining text and original record timestamps. With personalization ON, explicit additions/corrections use a Main tool and actual results. An unrelated durable fact supplied with deletion can still be remembered; the deleted target is excluded. Memory/history/private recovery labels are hidden, and the model generates its own response wording.
documents.s: Can information persist across a new chat_id?

documents.t: They cannot change service policy. One system message may provide lower-priority auxiliary instructions to the current request's Main Agent. It is excluded from graph messages and checkpoints and is not automatically inherited by subagents, the Evaluator, or compactor. temperature, top_p, max_tokens, max_completion_tokens, frequency_penalty, seed, stop, and generation_config are accepted for compatibility but discarded before validation. Callers choose the response transport using stream.
documents.s: Can system, temperature, or max_tokens change Agent policy?

documents.t: No. /workspace is private to user_id:chat_id. PostgreSQL checkpoints preserve it across requests and API processes for that thread, but not for a new chat or another user. Deployment assets/skills and assets/agents are separate shared sources. Only permitted assets appear read-only under /skills and /agents; they are not copied into the workspace.
documents.s: Can another user or chat see Agent files?

documents.t: No. /workspace holds internal drafts and analysis; there is no download endpoint or artifact card. Requested results must appear in the final chat body. File work may appear as [Tool] write_file; details OFF hides that notice but keeps execution.
documents.s: Can users download files created by the Agent?

documents.t: No. The filesystem is a default-deny virtual view of /workspace, /runtime, /memories, /skills, and /agents, not the host /. /runtime is a private framework namespace. Models can target only exact conversation-provided paths under /runtime/conversation_history/<artifact> and /runtime/large_tool_results/<artifact>. Writes, root browsing, arbitrary namespaces, relative paths, and traversal are denied. /memories/MEMORY.md is the current user's read-only long-term Memory and is unavailable for ordinary access with personalization OFF. Shell/execute, assets/mcp_server.json, and unrouted host files are not exposed. Backend and permission checks deny writes to /skills, /agents, and /memories.
documents.s: Can the Agent run a shell or read real pod files?

documents.t: Find the user's run_id in /v1/runs, then request its evidence. Observations contain actual execution inputs and outputs. Look for type="tool" with the search tool name: input holds the query and output holds retrieved results. Results remain sanitized JSON-safe values rather than arbitrarily truncated previews.
documents.s: How do I inspect RAG results used in Chat?

documents.t: Read the nested evidence tree. Each Main/subagent Agent's observations contains its models, tools, Skills, and nested agents in execution order. Search executed by a subagent { "type": "agent", "name": "researcher", "observations": [ { "type": "tool", "name": "rag_search", "input": {"query": "causes of deployment delays", "index": "rag-index"}, "output": {"results": [{"title": "Deployment Delay Overview", "score": 0.82}]} } ] } This tool belongs to researcher because it is nested under that Agent. Skills and models use the same ownership structure; clients need not reconstruct a public tree by joining separate IDs.
documents.s: How do I identify the Agent that executed a tool or Skill?

documents.t: Authorization uses the effective request's orch.rag_params.permission_groups. Resource Enforcement RAG retrieval Groups are sent to the backend to restrict searchable documents. MCP server/tool A declared non-empty access.permission_groups must intersect request groups. Absent or empty declarations are public. Skill The same group intersection rule applies. Agent The same group intersection rule applies.
documents.s: How are MCP, tool, and RAG permissions applied?

documents.t: They are exact strings used for RAG, MCP, Skill, and Agent authorization. Trusted callers use request groups directly; System/Sub frontends and personal API callers merge them with Permission API value fields queried using the normalized user_id. Additional personal API groups are intentionally allowed. A blank Permission URL skips API and cache access and uses request groups. A configured failure does not become OFF. Authentication OFF still preserves groups and ownership. Group comparison uses an unordered exact-string set(); do not assume normalization of case, whitespace, or Unicode.

They determine both searchable documents and visible MCP servers, Skills, and Agents. { "orch": { "rag_params": { "permission_groups": ["EXAMPLE_READERS", "EXAMPLE_REVIEWERS"], "index": "rag-index" } } } These are example groups, not mandatory fixed values. Send the actual signed-in user's groups from your permission system.

It selects candidate search corpora. A UI sends its selected value; direct API clients send orch.rag_params.index or Search index_name. Selecting an index does not make every chunk available to generation. The backend also intersects each uploaded chunk's groups with request groups. For example, rag-a,rag-b with only example-team can search only chunks in those indices that permit example-team. An index in a payload or database is not proof that all its chunks contributed to the answer.

Search tools forward request groups to the RAG API. A user with only example-team receives only documents permitted to that group. Runtime does not expand permissions or append unauthorized documents after receiving results.
documents.s: How do groups affect RAG search?

documents.t: An absent or empty access.permission_groups is public. A non-empty declaration requires at least one exact intersection with request groups; otherwise the asset is not a model candidate. For example, an MCP requiring restricted-team is absent from a request containing only example-team.
documents.s: How are MCP, Skills, and Agents shown or hidden?

documents.t: With authentication ON, issue an active Key with binding_field=send_system_name and the base system name as binding_value. No separate allowlist or redeployment is needed. A medic_test caller binds its Key to medic. OFF accepts calls without Key checks and returns 404 feature_disabled from Key management. Existing Key records are retained.
documents.s: Does registering a new System require redeployment?

documents.t: Yes. Several Keys may be active simultaneously and have independent expiry, verification, and revocation. For rotation, POST the new Key, switch the consumer, then DELETE the old Key. POST does not revoke existing Keys.
documents.s: Can several Keys share a binding?

documents.t: No. PATCH changes expires_at only on an active Key. Expired/revoked Keys return 409 api_key_not_active; POST a new credential. Repeated DELETE on a revoked Key is a 204 no-op and preserves the original revoked_at.
documents.s: Can PATCH reactivate an expired or revoked Key?

documents.t: Yes. Runtime skips the checkpoint-matching prefix and adds only the new suffix. Native compaction creates a summary projection and recent tail according to model capacity. Missing details can be recovered internally using grep and targeted read_file on thread-private /runtime/conversation_history/** archives. Clients do not manage these paths. Merely exceeding a compaction trigger does not reject the transcript; retrying a failed request also avoids duplicating checkpointed input. If the single latest user message exceeds provider context capacity, compaction of history cannot fix it. Split it and keep chat_id with a fresh x_request_id.
documents.s: Can I send a large transcript in the same conversation?

documents.t: Symptom Common cause Check/action 400 invalid_identity Missing orch, blank user, or literal user_id. Send a meaningful opaque user identifier; dots are irrelevant. 403 send_system_name_not_allowed _test appended to a trusted name or a reserved System sender. Personal callers omit sender or use exact api; Systems use a non-reserved base-name Key. 403 api_key_binding_mismatch Submitted Key binds to another sender/user. Inspect that Key's binding_field and binding_value. 400 invalid_identity with valid user Nil chat_id/x_request_id. Send non-nil UUIDs; malformed syntax returns 422. Unknown model ID absent from catalog. Use /v1/models IDs. 409 duplicate_request Reused request ID in the same session. New question → new UUID; retry IDs prevent work but do not replay responses. 409 session conflict Previous stream remains active. Wait for its completion. Too few results Empty/incorrect groups. Check DS permission mapping and payload. Wrong corpus Incorrect index. Check /v1/indices. HITL does not continue New chat_id used for the answer. Preserve chat ID; create a new request ID. HITL phases share a Langfuse trace Historical interaction-based traces or old trace seed. Reproduce a new interaction and compare per-run traces with PG phases. Old traces are not split retroactively. Invalid run cursor Cursor reused with different filters. Preserve the original query conditions. Upstream timeout/unavailable RAG/provider not responding. Check dependency health and existing timeout configuration. 409 run_not_terminal No terminal outcome yet. Wait for completion, HITL, or failure before detail/evidence. Observability unavailable Langfuse artifact unreadable despite terminal summary. Check URL, keys, worker, and ingestion delay separately from Chat availability. context_overflow Still over capacity after forced compaction. Split a large latest input; preserve chat ID with a new request ID. Same HITL question repeats Wrong chat ID or older runtime recreated the interrupted task. Resume the same chat with a new request ID and update runtime.
documents.s: What should I check after an error?

documents.t: STREAM_PROGRESS_DETAILS_ENABLED=false hides Tool/MCP, Skill/Agent, processing, and HITL labels. Answer text, heartbeat, compaction, actual HITL questions/options, and required errors remain. Execution, persistence, observability, and HITL remain active. Raw model reasoning is never exposed, even with details ON.
documents.s: What remains when detailed progress is OFF?

documents.t: Initial discovery failure of a valid server excludes only that server. Classified invocation failures return as tool results; two consecutive failures block the affected tool or server from both exposure and dispatch. Invalid arguments, successful empty results, cancellation, and HITL do not count. Existing safeguards against repeating unavailable calls and exceeding execution limits remain. The first request after 600 seconds from completed discovery retries registered servers. Successful discovery replaces the full list/definitions; an authoritative empty list removes tools. Failure preserves the last known good list and blocked state. Adopted recovery permits new requests; active requests retain their pinned definitions and block state. Configuration-file changes require a restart.
documents.s: Do repeated MCP failures stop the conversation?

documents.t: DEFAULT_LOCALE=ko|en selects server notices; TIMEZONE selects time interpretation and presentation. Defaults are ko and Asia/Seoul. Notice-language changes require restart, but TIMEZONE is fixed at first deployment. Preserve existing Korean records; deploy other regions independently. Model answers, external text, and machine-readable fields are not automatically translated. Docusaurus has its own language menu, independent of server settings. Documentation-only DOCS_ROOT_LOCALE=ko|en selects its deployment root, default ko; both languages are built. Naive time input uses the deployment zone. Ambiguous/nonexistent DST times require an explicit UTC offset.
documents.s: Where do I change language and timezone?

documents.t: Make one Chat request to confirm that Agent Runtime responds. Read the usage guide for field meanings and the API reference for endpoint response details.

Base URL environment export AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE=<agent-runtime-api-base-url> Check the model and index catalog first. Catalog requests curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/models" curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/indices"

This example requests one complete non-streaming JSON response. Chat request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "<model-id-from-catalog>", "stream": false, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Explain the causes of deployment delays and recommended actions."} ], "orch": { "chat_id": "2b0e1c88-540d-4af7-85d8-b1e7f6fa865e", "x_request_id": "896cd7ad-8e3c-4c85-b918-a294d133c44e", "identity": { "user_id": "employee.one", "send_system_name": "ds_assistant" }, "rag_params": { "index": "rag-index", "permission_groups": ["example-team"] } } }' This example uses a caller configured as a trusted sender by the operator, so no key is required. See the development guide for trusted senders. With CALLER_AUTH_ENABLED=false, key, binding, and trusted-sender checks are skipped. Identity and data ownership remain enforced, and a configured Permission URL is applied independently. On a deployment with RAG OFF, leave the example index empty and use an available model for ordinary Chat. System/Sub Frontend callers send an active key bound to their base sender, without registering a separate allowlist environment variable. For example, send_system_name=medic_test uses a key bound to send_system_name=medic. System caller API Key header curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-api-key: <active-system-binding-key>" \ -d '<request-with-send_system_name>' Personal API callers omit the sender or use exact api, and send an active key bound to the request user_id in the same header. See API Key management for key lifecycle and Chat authentication for the resolution order. The final answer is in choices[0].message.content. finish_reason="stop" means completion; hitl means waiting for the user's answer to an additional question. A non-streaming agent failure returns HTTP 500 with the common error envelope, rather than a choices response. Public Chat responses omit top-level token usage. Chat response { "id": "chatcmpl-abc123", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 1783958400, "model": "<model-id-from-catalog>", "choices": [ { "index": 0, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "Deployment delays can ..." }, "finish_reason": "stop" } ], "loop": { "tool_calls": 1, "model_calls": 1, "stop_reason": "completed", "duration_ms": 900, "repeats_blocked": 0, "compaction": {"occurred": false, "count": 0, "cutoff_index": null} }, "orch": { "result_message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "Deployment delays can ..." }, "rag": { "source_urls": {}, "contexts": {}, "warn_type": null, "rag_decide_yn": false, "doc_images": {} } } } For long conversations, native compaction projects earlier history into a summary and recent tail. Public responses expose only numeric loop.compaction metadata, not the summary or private archive path. Even when the full transcript is large, the stored checkpoint prefix is not appended again; only the new suffix is processed. If the current user request itself exceeds the provider context, the caller must split it. See compaction policy for model capacity and native trigger rules. When a streaming compaction begins, a notice appears in the reasoning area. After the previous compaction completes and Main body/Tool/Skill/Agent work actually resumes, the next compaction can send another notice. Internal summarization or consecutive retriggers without real work do not rearm it. loop.compaction.count preserves the actual compaction count. Summary content is used only internally. orch.rag is an empty compatibility structure. Its emptiness does not imply that RAG did not run; read actual retrieval/tool evidence through Runs evidence. STREAM_PROGRESS_DETAILS_ENABLED=false hides detailed Tool/Skill/Agent/processing notices and the HITL label. It preserves the answer, heartbeat, compaction, actual HITL questions/options, and required errors. DEFAULT_LOCALE selects only fixed server notices in ko/en; it does not automatically translate model answers.
This guide explains the values callers must prepare for each Agent Runtime request. Start with Quickstart to make a first call, and use API reference for endpoint contracts.

Chat uses an OpenAI-compatible payload with additional orch metadata. messages contains the conversation the model reads. orch supplies session identity, permissions, search scope, and duplicate-request information. tip Call GET /v1/models and GET /v1/indices first, then use the values allowed by the deployment in your Chat request. Request body { "model": "<model-id-from-catalog>", "stream": true, "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Explain the causes of deployment delays and recommended actions."} ], "orch": { "chat_id": "2b0e1c88-540d-4af7-85d8-b1e7f6fa865e", "x_request_id": "896cd7ad-8e3c-4c85-b918-a294d133c44e", "identity": {"user_id": "employee.one", "send_system_name": "ds_assistant"}, "rag_params": {"index": "rag-index", "permission_groups": ["example-team"]} } }

messages is the user-visible conversation. At least one message is required; at most one system message is allowed. Its text is an auxiliary instruction for the current HTTP request's Main Agent. It cannot override the service prompt, runtime context such as Memory and the current time, identity, security, authorization, tools, or evidence policy. The system message is excluded from graph messages and checkpoint history. It does not carry over to another request with the same chat_id unless sent again. HITL resume uses only the current resume request's instruction. Multipart content joins text parts in order and ignores images as instructions; blank text supplies no instruction. It is not automatically forwarded to subagents, the Turn Evaluator, or the conversation compactor. Streaming does not change these rules. Clients may resend the full user-visible transcript for the same chat_id. The server excludes the prefix matching its checkpoint and appends only the new suffix. Editing old messages can break prefix matching and duplicate history, so keep previous messages intact. Retrying a failed request with the same transcript does not append a user message already in the checkpoint. After a successful response, the same sentence sent as a new request is a new user occurrence. A large transcript is not rejected merely for exceeding the compaction trigger. Native compaction uses the model profile's capacity to produce a summary and recent tail so execution can continue. Missing historical details can be retrieved from thread-private runtime archives; clients do not manage /runtime paths. This cannot repair a single current user request larger than the provider context: split that input into smaller requests. An ask_user call can define 1–3 questions, each with 2–4 options and at most one recommendation. Questions are answered one at a time. Non-blank free text outside the options is passed through unchanged. max_tokens, max_completion_tokens, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, seed, stop, and generation_config are accepted for client compatibility but discarded before validation. They cannot change Main Agent or Internal LLM settings. The caller-controlled transport setting is stream.

Value Source Rule Notes model /v1/models → data[].id Use the catalog value unchanged. Manage it in model selection or caller configuration. user_id Signed-in user identity Send a non-blank opaque identifier. Dots have no format significance. Identifies sessions, Permission API queries, and personal Key bindings. send_system_name Caller system name With authentication ON, use a configured trusted sender, System/Sub frontend name, or personal API api. Test systems may use <base>_test. OFF skips Key binding and trusted classification; the value remains the Usage source. permission_groups Caller-supplied groups Use directly when the Permission URL is absent; otherwise merge API value fields according to caller policy. Controls RAG and MCP/Skill/Agent exposure and execution. index /v1/indices Send one string. Chat accepts comma-separated values; blank selects configured public RAG indices. Blank Search Proxy index_name returns 422. chat_id Caller-generated UUID4 Create once per conversation and preserve it. Used for multi-turn Chat, HITL, and the thread workspace. x_request_id Caller-generated UUID4 Create for every new user request. Reuse only for a network retry of the same request.

user_id separates user sessions, Usage, tool context, long-term Memory, and past conversation ownership. Identity validation and ownership remain enforced with authentication OFF. Personalization OFF skips automatic Memory loading, injection, and storage; it preserves records, summaries, history access, and explicit deletion of the user's own Memory. With personalization ON, Main tools confirm explicit additions/corrections. A deletion turn may retain unrelated durable facts while excluding deletion targets. Internal management/lookup labels are hidden; narration and answers remain model-generated. danger Provide meaningful requester identifiers in user_id, chat_id, and x_request_id. Only surrounding whitespace is stripped from user_id. Blank values and the literal "user_id" return 400 invalid_identity; employee, employee.one, and employee.one.test are all valid. Missing orch or nil UUIDs fail identity validation. Malformed UUID syntax instead returns 422 validation_error from schema validation.

orch.identity.send_system_name records the Usage source and selects the Chat authentication path when CALLER_AUTH_ENABLED=true. OFF skips Key verification, binding checks, and trusted classification. Caller send_system_name Trusted internal caller Exact system name permitted by the operator System / Sub frontend Issued Key's binding base name; append _test for test calls Personal API Omitted, null, blank, or exact api medic_test binds to medic. The _test suffix is removed only after the exact trusted-sender check. See Developer guide for that boundary. A matching active Key permits a system without an additional allowlist. A personal Key paired with a System sender returns 403 api_key_binding_mismatch; personal clients must omit the sender or send exact api.

Groups are authorization data, not display labels. They affect RAG document access and MCP, Skill, and Agent exposure and execution. Trusted callers use the requested groups unchanged. Sub frontends and personal API callers authenticate the Key and binding, query the Permission API with the normalized user_id, and merge every string value with requested groups using a set() union. Allowing additional caller-supplied personal API groups is intentional. If PERMISSION_API_URL is blank, both API queries and cache access are skipped and request groups are used. A configured API failure does not switch the feature OFF. Empty groups do not grant all permissions; public assets follow their declarations. warning Group order is irrelevant. Whitespace, case, and Unicode are not normalized. The queried user_id is not implicitly added as a group; send it explicitly if needed. Boundary Effect RAG retrieval Filters search to documents the user can access. MCP visibility Only servers allowed by effective groups are exposed. Skill visibility Main Agent and subagents see only permitted Skills. Agent visibility Only permitted Agents become delegation candidates. Manifest interpretation Routers must use the actual deployment permission policy. Request fragment {"permission_groups": ["example-team", "restricted-team"]}

index selects a search corpus. Query the catalog for the deployment's allowed values. info The value is the backend index name, not a UI label. A UI can show a friendly name but must send the value returned by /v1/indices. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/indices" Response ["rag-index"] Chat accepts one index or comma-separated indices in one string. Blank selects all public indices configured by RAG_INDEX. If built-in search is OFF or there is no public RAG index, /v1/indices returns [] and direct Search/Probe return 404 feature_disabled. Chat and independent custom MCP servers remain available. A configured upstream failure is distinct from OFF and from a successful empty result. One index {"rag_params": {"index": "rag-index", "permission_groups": ["example-team"]}} Multiple indices {"rag_params": {"index": "rag-index,example-index", "permission_groups": ["example-team"]}} All indices {"rag_params": {"index": "", "permission_groups": ["example-team"]}} Input Chat orch.rag_params.index Search Proxy index_name Allowed single value Uses that index. Uses that index. Comma-separated values Keeps only allowlisted entries. All entries must be allowlisted; otherwise 422. Blank string Uses all configured public RAG indices. 422 index_name must not be empty. Wildcard Excluded from the allowlist selection. Rejected with 422. Chat silently excludes disallowed entries. Validate against /v1/indices before calling; enforce the catalog allowlist in the client if invalid indices must be detected, rather than expecting Search Proxy's error behavior from Chat.

This is the conversation thread ID for LangGraph checkpoints, hitl_pending, HITL resume, same-session single-flight protection, and the internal /workspace. tip Store chat_id with each conversation record so reopening, follow-up questions, and HITL answers continue the same conversation. Python import uuid chat_id = str(uuid.uuid4()) User action chat_id Start a conversation New UUID Follow up in that conversation Preserve the UUID Answer HITL Preserve the UUID Reopen a conversation Use its stored UUID Internal working files persist only for the same user_id:chat_id. A new chat cannot see the old workspace. Files are not downloadable artifacts; the result is delivered in the assistant message. A concurrent request for the same session may return 409 session conflict. Wait for the previous stream to end before sending another question. HITL spans multiple HTTP requests but belongs to one interaction. Clients only need to preserve chat_id and create a new x_request_id. The server manages each request's run_id, the initial interaction_id, previous parent_run_id, and zero-based phase_index.

This is the caller's per-request idempotency/correlation ID. Internally and in PostgreSQL it is normalized to request_id. warning Create a new UUID for every new user question. Reusing it may return 409 duplicate_request. A network retry may reuse it to prevent duplicate work, but the server does not replay the earlier response: it closes the retry with 409. Python import uuid x_request_id = str(uuid.uuid4()) Situation x_request_id New question New UUID Network retry of the same question Reuse to prevent duplicate work and handle 409 New question after stopping New UUID Submit a HITL answer New UUID Refresh may resubmit a request Prevent duplicate submission in the UI A previously used ID within the same deduplication scope returns 409 duplicate_request, meaning the workload was not executed twice.

An Agent asset defines a Subagent for focused review or analysis. Users do not select it directly. Main can delegate independent research, narrow reviews, or draft checks that can be completed from a task prompt.

Agent directory assets/ agents/ evidence-reviewer.md Operators manage the physical asset path. The runtime mounts only permitted definitions read-only at /agents/<name>.md. Reading a definition and executing a Subagent are separate capabilities. The runtime control plane still constructs execution candidates and tool access; copying Markdown into the workspace does not activate an Agent. Agent definition --- name: evidence-reviewer description: Review evidence-backed answers for missing assumptions and caveats. skills: - evidence-review tools: - mcp__retriever__rag_search access: permission_groups: - ORG_PROCESS --- You are a focused evidence reviewer. Check whether the draft answer identifies the relevant facts, assumptions, and evidence gap. Return concise private guidance to the main agent. ORG_PROCESS illustrates the frontmatter format. Use groups from the deployment's actual authorization policy.

Field Meaning name Defaults to the Markdown filename stem. description Required; Main and /v1/manifest use it to understand the Agent. skills A nonempty list opens the permission-filtered native /skills source. It is not currently a per-name preload or allowlist. tools Only canonical names present in the registry are passed to the Subagent. Unknown names are omitted. ask_user and delete_user_memory are excluded even if declared. access Restricts exposure by permission group. Body Subagent system prompt. The runtime constructs a general-purpose Subagent alongside asset-defined Agents. The HITL tool ask_user is not exposed directly to Subagents; Main decides whether to ask the user for additional information. Explicit deletion of the owner's Memory through delete_user_memory is also restricted to Main. STREAM_PROGRESS_DETAILS_ENABLED=false hides only the [Agents] notice and preserves delegation. general-purpose is a runtime-generated helper, not an assets/agents/*.md inventory entry. Consequently, general-purpose delegation may work even when capabilities.agents is empty because no Agent asset exists.

MCP servers come from assets/mcp_server.json or builtin configuration. If the file exists, an explicitly empty mcpServers is respected rather than replaced with defaults. Without a file, active RAG/DS settings select builtin retriever and ds_retriever candidates. An absent RAG URL disables only builtin search; custom MCPs are independent. RAG-only indices select retriever, DS-only indices select ds_retriever, and both select both, while respecting enabled=false. Users do not call MCP tools directly. Supply correct Chat orch metadata so the runtime exposes only tools permitted by configuration and authorization.

Server Representative tool Purpose retriever mcp__retriever__rag_search Ordinary retrieval over RAG indices. retriever mcp__retriever__deep_search Deeper search strategies for RAG questions. ds_retriever mcp__ds_retriever__ds_rag_search DS index retrieval. Its current asset has includeInManifest=false, so it can be available in Chat while absent from the manifest. Canonical tool names use mcp__<server_name>__<tool_name>. Builtin implementations separate server-specific code from shared helpers. Bundled MCP server layout app/mcp_servers/ _common/ retriever.py search_strategy.py retriever/ server.py deep_search.py ds_retriever/ server.py _common/ holds shared RAG gateway, rerank, result-size policy, and strategy descriptions. Deep Search is specific to the RAG retriever and lives in retriever/deep_search.py.

MCP configuration { "mcpServers": { "retriever": { "transport": "stdio", "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "app.mcp_servers.retriever.server"], "env": { "RAG_API_URL": "${RAG_API_URL}", "RAG_API_KEY": "${RAG_API_KEY}", "RAG_X_DEP_TICKET": "${RAG_X_DEP_TICKET}", "INDEX": "${RAG_INDEX}" }, "requestScopedInjection": { "body": [ {"from": "permission_groups", "to": "permission_groups"}, {"from": "index", "to": "index", "overwrite": false}, {"from": "chat_id", "to": "chat_id"}, {"from": "request_id", "to": "request_id"}, {"from": "user_id", "to": "user_id"} ] }, "enabled": true, "includeInManifest": true }, "external_http": { "transport": "http", "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp", "requestScopedInjection": { "body": [ {"from": "permission_groups", "to": "permission_groups"}, {"from": "index", "to": "index", "overwrite": false} ], "header": [ {"from": "user_id", "to": "X-User-Id"}, {"from": "request_id", "to": "X-Request-Id"}, {"from": "chat_id", "to": "X-Chat-Id"} ] }, "enabled": true, "includeInManifest": true } } }

An entry's access.permission_groups is an exposure allowlist. Missing access or empty groups makes the server public. Otherwise at least one group must overlap with Chat's orch.rag_params.permission_groups before the runtime loads it. This is application-owned metadata used to filter servers before graph creation, not a payload sent to the MCP endpoint. Unauthorized tools are omitted from the model and rejected by dispatch even if the caller knows their canonical name. Setting Responsibility Example enabled Include/exclude the server entirely; default true. Set false to disable an MCP. includeInManifest Expose Router inventory without changing execution availability. Use false for internal-only MCPs. access.permission_groups Restrict server/tool visibility. Expose a server only to restricted-team. requestScopedInjection Populate tool arguments (body) or HTTP MCP headers (header). Inject ACLs or correlation IDs. timeout Tool-call timeout, default 60 seconds and explicitly 60 in builtin assets. Stdio uses a host wrapper; HTTP/streamable also passes it to the adapter connection. Increase only for a server whose normal operation needs longer. sse_read_timeout Idle event-read timeout after a streamable/SSE connection opens; adapter default 300 seconds. Set a different event-read limit for a particular server. enabled=false removes a server from both Chat and manifest. includeInManifest=false preserves Chat availability while hiding only inventory. Stdio timeout is not passed as an SDK connection argument; Agent Runtime wraps tool execution with it. HTTP/streamable uses it for both adapter connection and tool execution. Separately, MCP_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT bounds each server's entire discovery. Manifest can return a successful partial inventory excluding slow or failed servers. Initial Chat discovery excludes only failed servers and continues with healthy ones; no specific retriever tool name is required. Temporary failure of a valid external server is distinct from invalid local configuration, which is not silently treated as OFF. Chat keeps a last-known-good catalog per server. The first request after 600 seconds from the completed discovery attempt checks again. Failed servers retain their catalog; successful servers replace the complete list, including an authoritative empty list. A name, description, or input-schema change requires a new graph. No background refresh occurs without a request. Server entries and access-policy changes require process restart.

Situation Behavior Two consecutive connection/session failures Block all tools from that server. Two consecutive execution timeouts, structurally confirmed schema mismatches, or backend failures for one tool Block that tool and retain its siblings. Invalid arguments, request-specific authentication refusal, successful empty results, cancellation, or HITL Do not count as shared MCP failures. Successful discovery and adoption after the next 600 seconds Give new requests another opportunity; recovery applies even if the catalog is unchanged. Failed discovery or failed graph candidate construction Preserve the adopted graph/state and wait for the next 600 seconds. Both model exposure and actual dispatch enforce blocks for Main, Subagents, and additional execution. A failure is returned as a Tool result with the matching tool_call_id, allowing the agent to choose another tool or improve its answer. An external tool failure does not automatically stop the entire workflow, and uncertain writes are not automatically replayed. In-flight results are handled, but a late success does not immediately reopen a block. Requests pin their graph and availability generation. A tool blocked within one request is not reopened midway by another request's recovery. Late results from older generations cannot contaminate new ones. Only matching connection/auth scopes share failures. Fixed built-in RAG/DS connections retain failure counts and blocks across requests; correlation arguments do not reset them. Custom dynamic body/header injection retains request-local isolation. Structurally classified external failures do not spend LoopGuard's global mistake budget; ignored blocks, invalid arguments, and execution limits remain protected. Failure classification preserves the original remote diagnostic result. Blocked calls return the recorded failure domain/cause without transport or another external failure. Large evidence uses existing offload and bounded reads instead of arbitrary truncation. Stdio commands python and python3 use the API process's Python executable. Running the API in .venv therefore runs child MCPs there too. Explicit custom commands, absolute paths, and other launchers are preserved. sse_read_timeout measures inactivity between connection events, not total tool execution time. Builtin assets use the adapter's 300-second default without specifying another value.

requestScopedInjection is an object with body and header destinations, not an array. A from source can be a normalized Chat body field or an inbound HTTP header, supporting body→body, header→body, body→header, and header→header. Header destinations are supported only for HTTP/SSE transports; stdio/websocket header injection is a configuration error. Source Example body[].to Example header[].to Meaning permission_groups permission_groups Unsupported (list) RAG access filter index index X-Index Search indices request_id request_id X-Request-Id Downstream correlation user_id user_id X-User-Id User logging/filtering header[].to is the actual downstream HTTP header name. Map normalized user_id to a hyphenated name such as X-User-Id; snake_case belongs to body sources and destinations. Header names are case-insensitive, so X-User-Id, x-user-id, and X-USER-ID are equivalent. Prefer readable canonical names in configuration. overwrite: false preserves existing tool arguments or static headers, such as an agent's narrowed index or a fixed authentication header. Header destination matching is case-insensitive. warning If the same source occurs in both normalized body and inbound headers, the server rejects the ambiguity rather than choosing precedence. Do not send a user_id header alongside a from: user_id body source. Header destinations accept only scalars: put list-valued permission_groups in body injection and use scalar user_id, chat_id, request_id, or model for headers.

No separate setting selects MCP tools for evidence. Executed tools appear as Langfuse tool observations and can be read with JSON-safe input/output, errors, and agent ownership through Runs evidence. Tool input omits only the top-level framework-injected runtime; real arguments such as query, index, and permissions remain. Embedded tool descriptions/JSON schema in public model input are internal configuration and omitted. Actual Tool result messages and observation outputs remain available. Evidence request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000/evidence" Ownership is expressed by nesting: the closest containing type="agent" node owns the tool. Consumers do not need to match separate parent IDs.

A Skill is an instruction bundle that supplies a working method or review criteria. Users do not select Skills directly. Supply accurate permission_groups so the runtime can expose only permitted Skills.

Skill directory assets/ skills/ evidence-review/ SKILL.md Operators manage the physical asset path. The runtime filters Skills by the request's permission_groups and mounts permitted definitions read-only at Agent-visible /skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Agents do not read /assets/... or host paths directly. Write frontmatter and instructions in SKILL.md. SKILL.md --- name: evidence-review description: Review answer grounding against retrieved RAG evidence. access: permission_groups: - ORG_PROCESS --- Use this skill when a response depends on retrieved semiconductor process evidence. Check whether the answer separates evidence-backed facts from inference. ORG_PROCESS illustrates the frontmatter format. Use group names from your deployment's actual authorization policy.

Field Meaning name Defaults to the Skill directory name. An explicit name must match that directory. description Required; also appears in /v1/manifest at capabilities.skills[].description. access Restricts Skill exposure by permission group. Body The actual instructions read when the runtime uses the Skill. A missing access or empty access.permission_groups makes a Skill public. Otherwise, at least one group must overlap with the request's orch.rag_params.permission_groups before Main and permitted Subagents can see it. With STREAM_PROGRESS_DETAILS_ENABLED=false, hiding [Skill] progress does not change Skill permission checks or execution.

These internal operator endpoints issue, list, update expiry, and revoke Binding API Keys used by System/Sub frontends and personal API clients. CALLER_AUTH_ENABLED=false disables them with 404 feature_disabled, retains existing Key records, and skips Chat Key verification. danger There is no separate application credential for these endpoints. Ingress/network policy must restrict /internal/* to authenticated operators.

GET uses a key_ref query parameter; PATCH and DELETE use {key_ref} in the path. Both accept: UUID key_id 07da0100-661f-405a-be4f-3198a631438e 22-character public_key_id B9oBAGYvQFq-TzGYpjFDjg public_key_id is the internal UUID's 16 bytes encoded as unpadded Base64URL. It is public, not a secret. Both formats must pass canonical round-trip validation. warning The complete sk-<public_key_id>.<secret> cannot be a URL identifier. It returns 422 invalid_key_reference to keep secrets out of URLs and access logs. The full Key is 69 characters: sk-<22-character public_key_id>.<43-character secret>. PostgreSQL stores the UUID and an HMAC-SHA256 hash computed with a dedicated HKDF key derived from ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY; it stores neither the full Key nor secret. Chat strips surrounding whitespace from x-api-key before format validation. Internal whitespace, invalid prefix/length/Base64URL, and secret mismatch still return 401 invalid_api_key.

Usage binding_field binding_value Chat comparison Personal API user_id Opaque identity such as employee or employee.one orch.identity.user_id System / Sub frontend send_system_name Base name such as medic Sender with final _test removed System bindings reject whitespace, the _test suffix, and reserved values api and invalid_send_system_name. Test calls also use the base-name Key.

Retrieve RAG evidence for the Router's search_query. This endpoint does not execute the agent loop, HITL, or session memory. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/probe" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "metadata": { "chat_id": "afe26351-e2e5-4c70-8f4d-2a52f5dac7ac", "x_request_id": "6393d0c9-18ff-48b4-9f42-6cb687509587", "user_id": "employee.one", "permission_groups": ["example-team"] }, "context": { "original_query": "What is a deployment delay?", "search_query": "deployment delay causes", "is_multi_turn": false, "keywords": ["deployment", "delay"] }, "rag_options": { "max_results": 5 } }' Response { "metadata": { "timestamp": "2026-07-14T10:11:00+09:00", "chat_id": "afe26351-e2e5-4c70-8f4d-2a52f5dac7ac", "x_request_id": "6393d0c9-18ff-48b4-9f42-6cb687509587", "user_id": "employee.one", "permission_groups": ["example-team"], "original_query": "What is a deployment delay?", "search_query": "deployment delay causes" }, "evidence": { "rag": { "status": "ok", "results": [ { "id": "rag-1", "title": "Deployment Delay Overview", "content": "Deployment delay can occur when ..." } ] } } } metadata.chat_id and metadata.x_request_id must be UUIDs. Probe creates no Chat usage-ledger row and has no persistent dedup store. Repeating the same user_id:chat_id:x_request_id therefore executes both RAG workloads. Probe strictly rejects unknown fields. context can include optional conversation_summary, topic, and intent; rag_options.max_results ranges from 1 to 20. The server uses the Router's search_query unchanged and calls retrieve-cc over all configured RAG indices. RAG and rerank share one PROBE_TIMEOUT budget. On rerank failure or budget exhaustion, preserve the original RAG order. An absent builtin RAG URL or public RAG index returns 404 feature_disabled. A successful active RAG response with no hits produces evidence.rag.status="empty". Probe safely projects only title/content; upstream scores, URLs, and document IDs are omitted.

Evidence preserves execution results while excluding fixed internal settings. Runs is an operator/debugging API for status, loop telemetry, Main/subagent structure, and exact observation inputs/outputs. It is not a user answer replay API. tip Start with POST /v1/runs to find a run_id, then fetch detail and evidence. If you know request_id, filter Usage first and then inspect the run summary.

Lists a user's run summaries by deployment-zone time range and cursor. The list does not include full answers, provider traces, or retrieved document bodies. Field Meaning user_id Required user identity; retrieves that user's newest limit runs. from Start time. Accepts dates, minute/second datetimes, ISO T, Z, and offsets. Naive values use TIMEZONE. to End time with the same formats; explicit offsets retain their meaning. limit 1–100, default 20. cursor Next-page token; resend exactly as provided. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/runs" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "user_id": "employee.one", "from": "2026-07-14", "to": "2026-07-15", "limit": 20 }' Response { "items": [ { "run_id": "run_01J00000000000000000000000", "user_id": "employee.one", "chat_id": "2b0e1c88-540d-4af7-85d8-b1e7f6fa865e", "request_id": "896cd7ad-8e3c-4c85-b918-a294d133c44e", "created_at": "2026-07-14T10:12:00+09:00", "status": "completed", "model": "<model-id-from-catalog>", "stream": true, "interaction_id": null, "parent_run_id": null, "phase_index": 0 } ], "query": {"user_id": "employee.one", "from": "2026-07-14", "to": "2026-07-15"}, "page": {"limit": 20, "returned": 1, "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null} } The database filters by user_id before ordering created_at DESC, run_id DESC and limiting results. It does not fetch global recent runs and then filter the user. HITL field Meaning interaction_id null for ordinary runs; initial HITL uses its own run_id, and resumes use that initial ID. parent_run_id null initially; previous phase's run ID on resume. phase_index Starts at 0 and increases with each resume. Naive range values use TIMEZONE. With default Asia/Seoul, from: "2026-07-14" starts at midnight, and to: "2026-07-15" includes that entire day. to: "2026-07-14 10:30" includes that minute. Day boundaries account for the zone's DST. Ambiguous/nonexistent datetimes require an offset. Response timestamps use the deployment zone's offset.

When page.has_more=true, the response includes page.next_cursor. Preserve user_id, from, to, and limit; add only cursor for the next page. First page response excerpt { "items": [ {"run_id": "run_01J00000000000000000000002"}, {"run_id": "run_01J00000000000000000000001"} ], "query": {"user_id": "employee.one", "from": "2026-07-14", "to": "2026-07-15"}, "page": { "limit": 2, "returned": 2, "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "eyJ2IjoxLCJxIjoi..." } } Next page request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/runs" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "user_id": "employee.one", "from": "2026-07-14", "to": "2026-07-15", "limit": 2, "cursor": "eyJ2IjoxLCJxIjoi..." }' Next page response excerpt { "items": [ {"run_id": "run_01J00000000000000000000000"} ], "query": {"user_id": "employee.one", "from": "2026-07-14", "to": "2026-07-15"}, "page": {"limit": 2, "returned": 1, "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null} } warning Do not interpret or modify cursors. Changing any query field while reusing one returns 422. Restart from the first page without a cursor when changing filters.

Returns one run summary, loop telemetry, and the Main/subagent execution tree. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000" Response { "run": { "chat_id": "2b0e1c88-540d-4af7-85d8-b1e7f6fa865e", "request_id": "896cd7ad-8e3c-4c85-b918-a294d133c44e", "created_at": "2026-07-14T10:12:00+09:00", "status": "completed", "model": "<model-id-from-catalog>", "stream": true, "interaction_id": null, "parent_run_id": null, "phase_index": 0 }, "loop": { "tool_calls": 2, "model_calls": 3, "stop_reason": "completed", "duration_ms": 12400, "repeats_blocked": 0, "compaction": { "occurred": true, "count": 1, "cutoff_index": 37 } }, "execution_summary": [ { "type": "agent", "name": "main", "observations": [ {"type": "model", "name": "main"}, {"type": "tool", "name": "rag_search"}, {"type": "skill", "name": "policy-research"}, { "type": "agent", "name": "researcher", "observations": [ {"type": "model", "name": "researcher"}, {"type": "tool", "name": "deep_search"}, {"type": "model", "name": "researcher"} ] }, {"type": "model", "name": "main"} ] } ], "links": { "self": "/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000", "evidence": "/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000/evidence" } } run comes from PostgreSQL, loop from that run's Langfuse run.artifact, and execution_summary from semantic observations. Public detail excludes user_id and model/tool inputs/outputs. Discover a user's runs using the PostgreSQL-backed list, then fetch the selected ID's detail/evidence. The root is the Main Agent; its observations preserve execution order. A sequence glob → ls → glob appears in that order. Each subagent call becomes one nested type="agent" node at its execution position, so repeated calls to the same named Agent are separate nodes. Evidence contains actual inputs and outputs. Location Interpretation run.status completed, hitl, or failed in detail. running appears only in list; detail is not yet available. loop.tool_calls Framework tool invocation count. loop.model_calls Model calls, including continuations/retries. loop.repeats_blocked Repeated tool calls blocked. loop.compaction Native compaction in this request: occurred, actual count, and latest cutoff_index. execution_summary Agent ownership and ordered model/tool/Skill execution without inputs/outputs. List and evidence contain no loop. Compaction metadata appears only in Chat terminal/non-stream responses and Runs detail. Its count is actual native compaction occurrences. After a completed cycle and meaningful Main work, Chat can announce another compaction in the same request. Immediate retriggers without work suppress duplicate notices without reducing the count. Overflow remaining after forced compaction has stop_reason=context_overflow. Native summary bodies, archive paths under /runtime/conversation_history/**, and raw history remain private trace/state and are excluded from public Runs/evidence. Raw tool_calls can include subagent task and Skill read_file. Semantic projection represents those as agent and skill, so counting public tool nodes need not equal the raw counter. Older artifacts missing the entire loop.compaction key receive {"occurred": false, "count": 0, "cutoff_index": null}. An existing malformed object with missing count or private fields such as summary_text/file_path fails public projection rather than being silently repaired.

Returns Langfuse semantic Main/subagent, model, tool, and Skill observations. It does not expose live evidence before a run becomes terminal. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000/evidence" Response { "run_id": "run_01J00000000000000000000000", "observations": [ { "type": "agent", "name": "main", "observations": [ { "type": "model", "name": "main", "input": {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Investigate deployment delays."}]} }, { "type": "tool", "name": "rag_search", "input": {"query": "causes of deployment delays"}, "output": {"results": [{"title": "Deployment Delay Overview", "score": 0.82}]} }, { "type": "agent", "name": "researcher", "observations": [ { "type": "model", "name": "researcher", "input": {"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "Review the causes independently."}]} }, { "type": "tool", "name": "deep_search", "input": {"query": "deployment delay verification"}, "output": {"results": [{"title": "Verification", "score": 0.91}]} }, { "type": "model", "name": "researcher", "output": "Here are the research findings." } ] }, { "type": "model", "name": "main", "output": "Here is the final answer." } ] } ], "page": {"returned": 8, "complete": true, "next_cursor": null}, "links": { "self": "/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000/evidence", "run": "/v1/runs/run_01J00000000000000000000000", "next": null } } Location Interpretation observations[] Main-rooted tree with owned execution and subagents in order. type="model" / name One LLM invocation and its owning Agent; name is not the provider model ID. input / output Sanitized JSON-safe values without arbitrary previews or resummarization. Only fixed internal settings are excluded; no per-observation detail calls are needed. error { "message": "..." } only for failed observations. Successful nodes do not repeat status fields. page Newly returned observation count, completion, and next cursor. Pagination is automatic by JSON size, with a 4 MiB soft page budget. Observations are never split. If adding the next one exceeds the budget, the response includes page.complete=false, page.next_cursor, and links.next; follow that link unchanged. Required Agent ancestors repeat on later pages, while page.returned counts only newly returned observations. A single observation over 8 MiB returns 413 observation_too_large without truncating it. Large JSON supports HTTP gzip.

Situation Detail/evidence Meaning No PostgreSQL run ID 404 run not found Run does not exist. Summary still running 409 run_not_terminal Terminal artifact is unavailable. Terminal artifact not visible Retries within configured deadline, then 503 observability unavailable Langfuse delay or write failure. Terminal summary and artifact ready 200 Detail/evidence can be read. Each HTTP request creates one LangGraph trace in Langfuse Sessions. A HITL question and each resume have distinct run_id traces, each with one run.artifact child. interaction_id, parent_run_id, and phase_index connect phases. Session turns remain oldest-first. Reads use the whole LANGFUSE_RUN_READ_TIMEOUT deadline; large evidence does not fail prematurely after an arbitrary fixed retry count.

Search Proxy exposes the RAG API through the Agent Runtime API boundary. It validates the RAG index allowlist, normalizes queries, and generates a request ID before forwarding to RAG, so integrating services do not need to call RAG directly. info Ordinary user interfaces do not need to call Search Proxy. Most searches happen through Chat runtime MCP tools. Search Proxy serves internal search tools and operational checks. When the builtin RAG URL or public RAG index is absent, all direct search APIs return 404 feature_disabled. Timeouts and failures of a configured integration are returned as errors, rather than being disguised as successful zero-result searches.

Request body { "index_name": "rag-index", "query_text": "deployment delay root cause", "permission_groups": ["example-team"], "num_result_doc": 5, "fields_exclude": ["v_merge_content_title"] } Field Meaning index_name One or more comma-separated RAG indices. Empty values, wildcards, and values outside the allowlist are rejected with 422. query_text Search query. Except for query-term, control/special characters are normalized into searchable text. permission_groups Groups used by the RAG backend for access filtering. num_result_doc Result count, default 30. Use 1–50 to match the RAG contract; the proxy does not clamp this range itself. fields_exclude Fields excluded from the RAG response, default ["v_merge_content_title"]. Responses include a server-generated X-Request-Id header. On backend success, the backend body and content type pass through unchanged. The detailed response body therefore follows the RAG API contract; Agent Runtime owns validation and operational logging. Search does not create rows in the Chat-only usage ledger. Correlate it through X-Request-Id and application logs/traces. Request schemas reject unknown fields. KNN/RRF/CC filter must be an object whose values are lists. Query-match operator accepts only uppercase OR or AND. On upstream errors, the private body is replaced with a safe common error envelope while preserving the HTTP status and X-Request-Id.

Endpoint Additional fields Use POST /v1/search/retrieve-bm25 — Keyword search and exact term matching POST /v1/search/retrieve-knn filter Semantic/vector search POST /v1/search/retrieve-rrf filter Rank fusion of BM25 and vector results POST /v1/search/retrieve-cc filter, bm25_boost, knn_boost Default RAG hybrid retrieval POST /v1/search/query-match field, operator BM25 token matching in a particular field POST /v1/search/query-term field Exact term matching in a particular field

Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/search/retrieve-cc" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "index_name": "rag-index", "query_text": "deployment delay remediation", "permission_groups": ["example-team"], "num_result_doc": 5, "filter": {}, "bm25_boost": 0.02531451142318286, "knn_boost": 7.980074401837717 }'

Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/v1/search/query-match" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "index_name": "rag-index", "query_text": "deployment delay", "permission_groups": ["example-team"], "num_result_doc": 5, "field": "title", "operator": "AND" }'

These endpoints check whether the API server is running and responds to requests. warning All three are shallow checks of the process's HTTP responsiveness. They do not probe PostgreSQL, RAG, the LLM gateway, or MCP dependencies. Chat may still fail even when these endpoints return 200.

The simplest server-response check. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/" Response { "message": "Agent Runtime API Server is running." } message follows DEFAULT_LOCALE. With ko, it returns Agent Runtime API 서버가 실행 중입니다. Machine-readable values such as status are not translated.
Use this for a deployment check or a load balancer health check. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/health" Response { "status": "OK" }
Currently this checks whether the metrics route responds; it does not expose an actual metric collection. Request curl "$AGENT_RUNTIME_API_BASE/metrics" Response { "status": "OK" }
